evidence.claim: Teardown refuses when any live byte or index-referenced path is not proven preserved in the harvest (reason=unpreserved-content, worktree stays on disk) and deletes only after a byte-level harvest match (reason=content-proven). Commit ancestry is never consulted: on the squash-merge state the branch reports AHEAD (ahead_count=1, not an ancestor despite the content being carried) and the known-broken naive ancestry mutant authorizes deletion while the content gate refuses - measured, not asserted.

probes.command: refused(unharvested-remainder); mutant-authorizes and gate-refuses on same squash state; deleted(harvest-matched)

negative_controls.description: Two sibling files on one checkout plus git add -A must stage both paths; the detector fires on that contamination mode.
negative_controls.bad_state_output: unit-a.txt and unit-b.txt both staged on shared index

negative_controls.description: Teardown of a shard whose unique bytes are nowhere else must refuse and leave the worktree on disk.
Squash-merge plus an uncommitted remainder: ancestry reports AHEAD (naive mutant would delete); content comparison refuses.
